entities.summary: Alonso III Fonseca was a Galician archbishop and politician of immense influence in 16th-century Spain. As Archbishop of Santiago de Compostela from 1507 and Archbishop of Toledo from 1523, he played a pivotal role in shaping the intellectual and spiritual landscape of the region. Fonseca was a key figure in the University of Santiago de Compostela, which became a hub for humanist scholarship and the arts. His tenure as archbishop was marked by significant events, including the 1523 Toledo Synod, which brought together prominent theologians and scholars to address issues of doctrine and faith. Fonseca's legacy extends beyond his administrative roles, as he was also a patron of the arts and a supporter of the Compostela Cathedral's restoration. The Compostela Cathedral, a testament to Fonseca's devotion to the city and its patronage of the arts, continues to be a symbol of the region's rich cultural heritage. Fonseca's remarkable achievements in the realm of religion and politics have left an indelible mark on the annals of history, cementing his place as one of the most important figures of his era.
